questions.q: Which three types of notes does Ahrens recommend?
questions.why: Lesson 1 names fleeting notes, literature notes and permanent notes.

questions.q: Where should fleeting notes be kept?
a: In a notebook or on paper, not in the slip-box
In the main slip-box, sorted by topic
In a digital folder arranged by date
questions.why: Lesson 1 says fleeting notes capture first ideas and stay outside the slip-box.

questions.q: What is the second slip-box used for?
a: Ideas and thoughts, the main and most valuable
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the second box holds ideas and is considered the main box.

questions.q: What should you do with fleeting notes after making permanent ones?
a: Copy them into the second box
questions.why: Lesson 1 advises storing permanent notes safely and discarding the fleeting ones.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest tackling a large writing project?
a: Break it into chunks and write a page a day
Write the whole draft in one sitting
questions.why: Lesson 3 says splitting work into smaller pieces makes completion more likely.
